# `aitbc agent-msg ping`

Ping a remote agent via WebSocket and wait for its PONG reply.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc agent-msg ping [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--agent` | text | `hub-coordinator` | no | Recipient agent ID to ping |
| `--sender` | text | `follower` | no | Sender agent ID (your agent ID for the WebSocket connection) |
| `--coordinator-url` | text | — | no | Agent Coordinator URL. Direct: http://localhost:8107. Via nginx on the hub: https://hub.example.net/agent (default: from config agent_coordinator_url) |
| `--timeout` | integer | `10` | no | Seconds to wait for a PONG reply |
| `--wallet` | text | — | no | Wallet to authenticate the stream with (mints an agent JWT via the coordinator login endpoint when --sender is bound to it) |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc agent-msg ping
```
